office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Stephen Bartels
incumbent.summary: Stephen Bartels of Eckerty, an Army veteran and Patoka Lake business owner, was chosen by a Republican caucus in November 2017 to fill the rest of Lloyd Arnold's term and has held House District 74 since [3]. He chairs the House Veterans Affairs and Public Safety Committee [4].
record: Committees: Veterans Affairs and Public Safety (chair), Courts and Criminal Code, and Public Policy; co-chair of the legislature's defense caucus (2025) [4]. In May 2026 Gov. Mike Braun picked him to chair the Indiana Defense Task Force [5].
2023: Sponsored HEA 1017, creating a prescription drug donation repository for uninsured or underinsured low-income Hoosiers [6].

2026: Authored HEA 1003, which sunsets or restructures more than 40 state boards and commissions [7]; authored HEA 1210, raising the property tax deduction for totally disabled veterans to 100% of their home's assessed value and adding other veteran credits [8]; sponsored SEA 227, making the Indiana State Police the lead agency for countering drones once federal authorization exists [9].

Voted yes on the 2025 budget conference report, HEA 1001 (April 25, 2025) [10]; was excused and did not vote on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law, on April 10, 2025 [11]. Was one of the Republicans who voted no on HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill, which passed the House 57-41 on Dec. 5, 2025 [12].

race_context: House District 74 covers all of Perry, Crawford and Spencer counties and parts of Dubois and Orange counties, per the House Republican caucus [4].
Bartels won 68.6% of the vote in 2024 [13]. He was unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary, and no Democrat appears in the primary results [13].
The Dubois County Free Press lists Stephen R. Bartels (R) and Lena Goffinet (D) on the Nov. 3 ballot [14].
Key differences: Goffinet has published no policy positions that we could find; her campaign website shows only a placeholder page [15].
No debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Lena Goffinet is the Democratic nominee; we found almost no published information about her background or positions [16, 15].
background: Her iVoterGuide profile lists no education, work or affiliation information [16].
path_to_ballot: Was not on the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary ballot; no Democratic primary for this seat is listed [13]. How she was nominated was not found.
on_incumbent: No statements about Bartels or the seat's record were found.
endorsements_finance: iVoterGuide lists an endorsement from the Spencer County Democrats [16].
gaps: Campaign website (hoosiersfirst.com) showed only a "Coming Soon" page when checked; Facebook and Instagram pages were not readable.
No news coverage was found in Perry, Spencer or Dubois county outlets reviewed.
How she reached the ballot (likely a Democratic ballot-vacancy caucus after the primary) is unconfirmed.

candidates.summary: Stephen Bartels has held the seat since November 2017 and chairs the House Veterans Affairs and Public Safety Committee [3, 4]. He was unopposed in the May primary [13].
background: Served 22 years in the military, retiring as a major, and nine years as an Indiana law enforcement officer [4].
Owns and operates Patoka Lake Marina and is owner and vintner of Patoka Lake Winery [4].
Former Crawford County Council president and former president of the Crawford County Tourism Board [4, 3]. Lives in Eckerty [4].
path_to_ballot: Was unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary [13].

items: Authored HEA 1210 (2026) expanding property tax relief for disabled veterans, saying it protects "their homes as a thank you for protecting ours" [8].
Authored HEA 1003 (2026) to consolidate state boards and commissions, saying it "strengthens and modernizes" how they are structured [7].
Sponsored SEA 227 (2026) on counter-drone authority, saying it "gives law enforcement the tools they need to stay ahead of emerging threats" [9].
Says defense-industry growth in southern Indiana is creating high-wage careers [5].
Voted no on the December 2025 congressional redistricting bill, HB 1032 [12].

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements about his challenger were found.
plans: As chair of the Indiana Defense Task Force, his 2026 bill directs state defense funding to match the task force's priorities [5].
gaps: No public statement explaining his no vote on HB 1032 was found.
No endorsements or fundraising totals were found.
